- Can product + pricing pick a recommended mapping per cloud (hosted-only vs dedicated vs private offers)?

- Are we OK to pilot AWS co-sell for a limited set of SKUs in Q2?

Target timelines from partners: AWS wants a pilot commitment by mid-March to make Q2 co-sell lists; Azure is flexible but needs packaging details for marketplace listing; GCP wants legal review up-front.

Thanks Karthik — good summary. My initial product suggestion (high-level):

- Starter (hosted-only): low-cost, fixed token limits, streaming, no dedicated GPU. Ship as Marketplace listing for AWS and Azure (hosted only).
- Scale (hosted + dedicated option): includes burst to Dedicated pools, KV-caching enabled, higher token limits; available as Marketplace SKU + private offer (AWS private offers supported).
- Enterprise (dedicated + managed/private offers): dedicated GPU pools, VPC/private deployment options, premium support and longer retention. Marketplace entry should be enterprise-only; for GCP we may list Enterprise only.

Region recommendation: start with US commercial regions (us-east-1, us-west-2) for the pilot — keep EU as \"coming soon\" until we have the PII/data residency checklist cleared.

Pricing notes: see attached azure_pricing_notes.docx for suggested Azure list prices (I used parity with AWS list, adjusted for marketplace fees). We should avoid per-region price divergence for launch.

Quick legal flags — please read before we commit to region/SKU strategy:

1) AWS co-sell and private offers: needs our ISV registration complete, plus a few commercial redlines (redistribution, indemnity caps). I've attached AWS's co-sell requirements we received (aws_co-sell_requirements.pdf).
2) Data residency: if we list a SKU that states \"EU availability\" we need SOC 2 + documented dataflows for PII; until security signs off, limit EU regions to "coming soon."
3) Azure Marketplace: their co-sell program requires an appended MSA addendum and certain revenue reporting; Azure's ISV co-sell paperwork can add 2-3 weeks.
4) GCP: they want marketplace terms included in our SOW; expect higher legal review time if we expose private offers.

I'll start drafting the minimum contractual language we need to ship for a pilot and will coordinate with Security for the residency checklist.

Karthik — thanks for the note and the matrix. Short answers below: 

1) Co-sell support: Yes — AWS will co-sell hosted SaaS offers and private offers that represent dedicated capacity, but you need to register the offer type correctly (SaaS vs AMI/Marketplace). For dedicated-managed capacity, we typically recommend the private offer route so you can control entitlements.

2) Region-limited private offers: Private offers can be constrained by region for commercial marketplaces; however, the public listing generally needs a consistent availability footprint. Many ISVs list in a subset of public regions and use private offers for region-specific enterprise deals.

3) Timeline: From complete submission to co-sell enablement we usually see 4–6 weeks (faster if the ISV registration and SOC2 paperwork are already in place).

Next steps: submit the co-sell registration form (https://aws.amazon.com/partner/programs/co-sell) and share the SKU matrix in the partner console. If you plan a private offer, we'll need entitlement/SSO details (JWKS endpoint) and the billing contact.

Happy to set a short call with the AWS SA team next week if that helps.

Best,
Mike Carroll
AWS Marketplace Partner Solutions
